workLog.phase: Measure the gate failure and trace every orphan
actions: Ran scan.py on default targets against clean main and got VERDICT: CRITICAL_FAIL with 32 findings across 12 spec files
Grouped findings by referenced entity: 24 point at one retired script, and the rest split across three more
Ran git log --diff-filter=D on each missing path to find the commit that removed it, rather than guessing whether a replacement exists
workLog.outcome: Every orphan traced to a deliberate deletion: #2187 retired the count validator, #3432 removed the bundle registry as dead code, #1141 migrated the traceability script to Python, #610 renamed the session-end validator

workLog.phase: Check whether the repo had already decided this question
actions: Found .agents/critique/001-fix-validate-sessionend-references-critique.md, which rejected an earlier plan for treating historical records as errors
Confirmed the current correction already lives in .claude/commands/build.md, which states the old marketplace count validator has been retired
Read every one of the 32 reference lines: each reads as narrative about what existed at authoring time, using words like existing and EXISTING, not new
workLog.outcome: Rewriting the specs would introduce anachronism the repo has already ruled against, and the correction a reader needs is already in current documentation

workLog.phase: Choose the narrower of the two escape hatches
actions: Read the directive table in the skill: file scope skips the whole file, line scope skips one line
Counted existing precedent with git ls-files: 39 line-scope directives and 29 file-scope already in the tree, four of them in the files being fixed
Chose line scope because the skill's own anti-pattern list warns that file scope on a spec masks real orphans, and these specs stay in the scan
workLog.outcome: 30 directives across 12 files, verified by diff to be pure suffix appends with no prose changed, and the gate now prints VERDICT: PASS
